notToBeConfusedWith.name: Rum
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Rum is usually distilled from molasses, a sugar-refining byproduct; cachaça is distilled from fresh-pressed sugarcane juice, which is a Brazilian legal requirement rather than a stylistic choice.

forms.label: Standard strength
forms.sourceNote: FoodData Central carries no cachaça-specific record; Brazilian law sets cachaça's bottled strength at 38-48% ABV, with most commercial brands landing around 39-43%, so 40% is adopted as the representative bottling. The kcal and carbohydrate figures are carried from Alcoholic beverage, distilled, rum, 80 proof (public domain) because energy in an unsweetened spirit is a function of its ethanol content alone, which is identical at the same ABV whatever the base material. Density is the spirit-40 class from density-classes.json rather than the rum record's own, since cachaça and rum are not the same liquid.
